[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +PEP 621 manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and its GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context. Action: run the read-only hosted
[codex] +   validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: preserve the run URL
[codex] +   and logs showing the effective shared policy, package identities, Action and
[codex] +   scanner lookups, and no fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +PEP 621 manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and its GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context. Action: run the read-only hosted
[codex] +   validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: preserve the run URL
[codex] +   and logs showing the effective shared policy, package identities, Action and
[codex] +   scanner lookups, and no fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] async function extractPackageFile(content, packageFile) {

[codex] 	} : null;

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +PEP 621 manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and its GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context. Action: run the read-only hosted
[codex] +   validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: preserve the run URL
[codex] +   and logs showing the effective shared policy, package identities, Action and
[codex] +   scanner lookups, and no fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +PEP 621 manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and its GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context. Action: run the read-only hosted
[codex] +   validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: preserve the run URL
[codex] +   and logs showing the effective shared policy, package identities, Action and
[codex] +   scanner lookups, and no fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +PEP 621 manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and its GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context. Action: run the read-only hosted
[codex] +   validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: preserve the run URL
[codex] +   and logs showing the effective shared policy, package identities, Action and
[codex] +   scanner lookups, and no fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +PEP 621 manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and its GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context. Action: run the read-only hosted
[codex] +   validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: preserve the run URL
[codex] +   and logs showing the effective shared policy, package identities, Action and
[codex] +   scanner lookups, and no fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] +          import re
[codex] +          from datetime import UTC, datetime

[codex] +
[codex] +
[codex] +          def normalized_name(value: str) -> str:
[codex] +              return re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", value).lower()
[codex] +
[codex] +

[codex] +          audit_status = int(os.environ["PIP_AUDIT_STATUS"])

[codex] +          audit_path = report_dir / "pip-audit.json"
[codex] +

[codex] +          audit_value = json.loads(audit_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
[codex] +          if not isinstance(installed_value, list):
[codex] +              raise ValueError("installed package evidence is not a JSON array")
[codex] +          if not isinstance(audit_value, dict) or not isinstance(
[codex] +              audit_value.get("dependencies"), list
[codex] +          ):
[codex] +              raise ValueError("pip-audit output has no dependency array")
[codex] +
[codex] +          installed = {
[codex] +              normalized_name(item["name"]): item["version"] for item in installed_value
[codex] +          }
[codex] +          reported = {
[codex] +              normalized_name(item["name"]): item["version"]
[codex] +              for item in audit_value["dependencies"]
[codex] +          }
[codex] +          if installed != reported:
[codex] +              missing = sorted(installed.keys() - reported.keys())
[codex] +              extra = sorted(reported.keys() - installed.keys())
[codex] +              mismatched = sorted(
[codex] +                  name
[codex] +                  for name in installed.keys() & reported.keys()
[codex] +                  if installed[name] != reported[name]
[codex] +              )
[codex] +              raise ValueError(
[codex] +                  "pip-audit did not report the exact installed dependency set: "
[codex] +                  f"missing={missing}, extra={extra}, version_mismatch={mismatched}"
[codex] +              )
[codex] +
[codex] +          vulnerable_dependencies = [
[codex] +              item for item in audit_value["dependencies"] if item.get("vulns")
[codex] +          ]
[codex] +          vulnerability_count = sum(
[codex] +              len(item["vulns"]) for item in vulnerable_dependencies

[codex] +              "vulnerability_count": vulnerability_count,

[codex] +              stream.write(

[codex] +              )
[codex] +              stream.write(f"Vulnerability records: {vulnerability_count}\n\n")
[codex] +              if vulnerability_count:

[codex] +                      "scheduled report.\n"
[codex] +                  )

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +PEP 621 manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and its GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context. Action: run the read-only hosted
[codex] +   validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: preserve the run URL
[codex] +   and logs showing the effective shared policy, package identities, Action and
[codex] +   scanner lookups, and no fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. This repository is PEP
[codex] +621, not Poetry, so its configuration disables Renovate's Poetry manager to
[codex] +prevent that manager from superseding the native PEP 621 manager. The PEP 621
[codex] +manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and the GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +The audit covers packages retained in the installed test environment. The
[codex] +isolated build environment used temporarily for `setuptools>=69` is not part of
[codex] +that installed set; Renovate extraction and hosted dependency-graph evidence are
[codex] +the update and advisory paths for that build requirement.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 19 records
[codex] +from three files: 13 PEP 621 declarations, five workflow records, and the
[codex] +regex-managed `pip-audit` pin. The PEP 621 set contained the Python lower bound,
[codex] +`setuptools`, and all 11 unbounded runtime/development requirements. Every
[codex] +unbounded requirement was retained with `unspecified-version`; this accurately
[codex] +prevents a fabricated routine update. Public PyPI lookups resolved `setuptools`
[codex] +and `pip-audit`, with no proposal because their current constraints or pin were
[codex] +already current.
[codex] +
[codex] +GitHub-backed Action and `actions/setup-python` lookups were deferred because no
[codex] +token was supplied. The Python release lookup also returned `no-result` after
[codex] +the anonymous GitHub GraphQL endpoint reported HTTP 403 rate-limit exhaustion.
[codex] +The run returned zero with no uncaught exception; these authenticated/rate-limit
[codex] +lookups remain pending Phase 12 and are not reported as successful coverage.
[codex] +

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. This repository is PEP
[codex] +621, not Poetry, so its configuration disables Renovate's Poetry manager to
[codex] +prevent that manager from superseding the native PEP 621 manager. The PEP 621
[codex] +manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and the GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] +tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] +The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] +
[codex] +- `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex] +  ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex] +  does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] +- Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex] +  checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex] +  requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] +- The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex] +  concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] +
[codex] +Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] +to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] +versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] +historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] +dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] +`.[dev]`, and records both JSON and `pip freeze --all` installed-version lists.
[codex] +This includes runtime and development dependencies but deliberately does not
[codex] +install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] +
[codex] +The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] +installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] +metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] +to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] +comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] +checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] +
[codex] +The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] +contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] +Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] +exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] +Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] +installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] +workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] +pull requests.
[codex] +
[codex] +The audit covers packages retained in the installed test environment. The
[codex] +isolated build environment used temporarily for `setuptools>=69` is not part of
[codex] +that installed set; Renovate extraction and hosted dependency-graph evidence are
[codex] +the update and advisory paths for that build requirement.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Credential-free local evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, a fresh Python 3.12.3 environment installed 34 third-party
[codex] +packages from the unchanged `.[dev]` declarations. Direct runtime selections
[codex] +were `httpx` 0.28.1, `jsonschema` 4.26.0, `playwright` 1.62.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5,
[codex] +`PyYAML` 6.0.3, `pytest` 9.1.1, and `referencing` 0.37.0. Direct development
[codex] +selections were `mypy` 2.3.1, `respx` 0.23.1, `ruff` 0.16.6, and `types-PyYAML`
[codex] +6.0.12.20260906.
[codex] +
[codex] +The standard JSON report covered all 34 installed third-party packages. It
[codex] +reported seven vulnerability records for the environment's `pip` 24.0 and no
[codex] +findings for the other 33 packages. This is time-specific installed-environment
[codex] +evidence, not a desired-version table or review-parity claim. Future comparisons
[codex] +must use advisory and package identities rather than assuming the count remains
[codex] +seven.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 19 records
[codex] +from three files: 13 PEP 621 declarations, five workflow records, and the
[codex] +regex-managed `pip-audit` pin. The PEP 621 set contained the Python lower bound,
[codex] +`setuptools`, and all 11 unbounded runtime/development requirements. Every
[codex] +unbounded requirement was retained with `unspecified-version`; this accurately
[codex] +prevents a fabricated routine update. Public PyPI lookups resolved `setuptools`
[codex] +and `pip-audit`, with no proposal because their current constraints or pin were
[codex] +already current.
[codex] +
[codex] +GitHub-backed Action and `actions/setup-python` lookups were deferred because no
[codex] +token was supplied. The Python release lookup also returned `no-result` after
[codex] +the anonymous GitHub GraphQL endpoint reported HTTP 403 rate-limit exhaustion.
[codex] +The run returned zero with no uncaught exception; these authenticated/rate-limit
[codex] +lookups remain pending Phase 12 and are not reported as successful coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 hosted and authenticated evidence handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +No GitHub, package-index, or Mend credentials are required or used during local
[codex] +preparation. The activation operator must complete and retain these checks:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: the trusted
[codex] +   hosted Renovate full dry run after the orchestration preset is published.
[codex] +   Scope: `pyproject.toml`, all workflow Actions and Python inputs, and the
[codex] +   `pip-audit` pin. Reason: published preset resolution and GitHub-backed Action
[codex] +   lookups require Phase 12 operator context; the local anonymous Python release
[codex] +   lookup exhausted its GitHub API limit and returned `no-result`. Action: run
[codex] +   the read-only hosted validation, then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof:
[codex] +   preserve the run URL and logs showing the effective shared policy, all 19
[codex] +   package identities, successful Action/Python/scanner lookups, and no
[codex] +   fatal/error output.
[codex] +2. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: manually
[codex] +   dispatch `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` from trusted `main`.
[codex] +   Scope: the then-current Python 3.12 `.[dev]` installation, `pip-audit`, and
[codex] +   PyPI advisory service. Reason: the workflow is not published during local
[codex] +   preparation, and hosted package/audit access has not been observed. Action:
[codex] +   dispatch without exposing the ephemeral GitHub token. Proof: preserve the run
[codex] +   URL, source revision, and complete seven-day artifact; verify exact installed
[codex] +   package/report parity and distinguish findings from operational failures.
[codex] +3. Repository: `budgetanalyzer/budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Check: GitHub
[codex] +   dependency graph and Dependabot alert settings. Scope: Python dependency and
[codex] +   advisory coverage. Reason: repository settings are administrator-owned.
[codex] +   Action: enable the graph and alerts, keep Dependabot version and overlapping
[codex] +   security-update pull requests disabled, and grant Renovate alert-read access.
[codex] +   Proof: retain sanitized setting and alert evidence and reconcile advisory
[codex] +   package identities with the `pip-audit` report, recording any unsupported
[codex] +   unbounded-requirement or transitive-package gap.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate discovery, Dependabot alerts, and `pip-audit` do not establish Python or
[codex] +package support lifecycles. Continue the quarterly upstream lifecycle review.

[codex] +## Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate configuration and the weekly/manual installed-environment `pip-audit`
[codex] +workflow are documented in
[codex] +[`docs/dependency-automation.md`](docs/dependency-automation.md). The workflow
[codex] +installs `.[dev]` in an isolated Python 3.12 environment and does not install
[codex] +browser binaries or contact a Budget Analyzer deployment. Automation remains
[codex] +inactive until the shared Phase 12 activation procedure is completed.
[codex] +
[codex]  Export the coverage artifact, including deferred admin operation status:
[codex]  
[codex]  ```bash
